name: Baked Japanese Sweet Potatoes with Miso Tahini Butter
description: Caramelized Japanese sweet potatoes topped with umami-rich miso tahini butter

timing.notes: Includes 45-60 minutes passive time in turned-off oven for caramelization

equipment.notes: Line with parchment paper for easy cleanup

equipment.alternative: Place potatoes directly on oven rack

ingredients.notes: Purple skin, white/yellow flesh - not orange American sweet potatoes
White (shiro) miso is milder - adjust to taste
Must be toasted sesame oil, not plain
Or maple syrup - balances the miso

prep_steps.instruction: Set up your staging area: get out a medium bowl for the compound butter, a small bowl for garnishes, your zester, and measuring spoons. Set the butter out to soften if not already.
prep_steps.notes: Soft butter is essential for smooth compound butter

prep_steps.instruction: Scrub the sweet potatoes under running water to remove any dirt. Pat dry.
prep_steps.notes: Japanese sweet potatoes have edible skin

prep_steps.instruction: Zest half of the lime into the medium bowl
prep_steps.notes: Only need zest from half the lime

prep_steps.instruction: Juice the lime half (about 1 1/2 tablespoons) and add to the bowl with the zest
Add softened butter, tahini, miso paste, toasted sesame oil, agave, and red pepper flakes to the bowl with the lime
prep_steps.notes: All compound butter ingredients go in the same bowl

prep_steps.instruction: Pick cilantro leaves from stems and place in small bowl with sesame seeds. Set aside for garnishing.
prep_steps.notes: Everything for the final garnish together

cook_steps.instruction: Lightly slash or prick the sweet potatoes several times with a sharp knife to allow steam to escape
cook_steps.warnings: This prevents potatoes from bursting in the oven

cook_steps.instruction: Place potatoes on parchment-lined baking sheet (or directly on oven rack with a pan below to catch drips)
Bake potatoes: 60 minutes for small, 75 minutes for medium, 85-90 minutes for large. Potatoes should be completely soft when pierced.

cues.visual: Skin is slightly wrinkled, caramelized syrup may leak from slits

cook_steps.warnings: Size varies - test with a knife for doneness

cook_steps.instruction: Turn off oven but keep potatoes inside with door closed for 45-60 minutes. This caramelizes the natural sugars.

cues.visual: Potatoes will look more wrinkled, may have caramelized syrup pooled around them

cook_steps.warnings: This step transforms good sweet potatoes into amazing ones - don't skip it

cook_steps.instruction: While potatoes rest in oven, make the compound butter: mash all ingredients in the medium bowl with a fork until very smooth and well combined

cues.visual: Smooth, creamy mixture with no lumps of miso
cues.aroma: Nutty, savory, with hint of lime

cook_steps.instruction: Taste the compound butter and adjust: add more miso for umami, more lime juice for brightness, or more sesame oil for nuttiness
If butter has become too soft/melty, refrigerate for 15-20 minutes until spreadable consistency

cues.visual: Butter holds its shape when scooped but spreads easily

cook_steps.warnings: Optional step - only if butter is too runny

cook_steps.instruction: If toasting your own sesame seeds: add to dry skillet over medium heat, toss occasionally until lightly golden

cues.visual: Seeds are light golden, a few may pop

cook_steps.warnings: Watch carefully - they go from toasted to burnt quickly

cook_steps.instruction: Remove sweet potatoes from oven. Slice each one open lengthwise.

cues.visual: Interior is creamy, golden-orange, may have caramelized spots

cook_steps.warnings: Potatoes are very hot - use a towel to hold them

cook_steps.instruction: Spread generous amount of miso tahini butter into each potato, letting it melt into the flesh

cues.visual: Butter melts and pools into the potato

finishing.instructions: Top each potato with toasted sesame seeds, a pinch or two of flaky sea salt, and fresh cilantro leaves from the small bowl. Zest a bit more lime directly over the top just before serving. Optional: sprinkle with vegan furikake or gomasio.
finishing.make_ahead: Compound butter can be made up to 5 days ahead and refrigerated. Bring to room temperature before using. Sweet potatoes are best baked fresh.
finishing.storage: Leftover potatoes keep refrigerated for 3 days. Store compound butter separately. Reheat potatoes in 350°F oven.

notes: Japanese sweet potatoes (murasaki) have purple skin and white/yellow flesh - they're drier and sweeter than orange American sweet potatoes
The 'rest in turned-off oven' step is the secret - it caramelizes the natural sugars
Compound butter ratio can be adjusted to taste - start with less miso and add more
Make extra compound butter - it's incredible on rice, roasted vegetables, or toast
